system: Session Inbox admission, submission and continuation scheduling
bounds: Two sessions in one workspace/account; one already-submitted A batch with a retained settlement; one B automatic batch/result; one Stop of B; at most two B starts to detect replay. One scanner fiber, a coalesced wake bit, a running-worker latch and per-session admission. No quiesce, host owner handoff, fresh-input replacement or native Agent process.
limits: Original scheduling slice is finite: two sessions, one retained A settlement, one B batch/input/Stop and at most two B starts; weak fairness and repeated wake opportunities, B never stopped in progress profile. Expanded slices and exact source limits are in expanded-coverage.json. Real replay uses production service/owner/repository/native SQLite, injected provider start and logger port. Native capacity fixture is not OS disk exhaustion. No full app/replication/authorization/native provider/device acceptance, unbounded refinement or whole-database-outage availability is proved. The sync commit contains every hash-verified product source; the separate verification commit follows it.

finding.cause: An unresolved A settlement aborts retrySettlements before scan reaches repo.pending; outer catch reports and returns to Queue.take. Every further wake retries A first and can abort again.

actions.RecordASettlement: service.ts settle: retain Map receipt before repository.settle; failed write stays retained and wakes scanner; execution-owner.ts finishWork observes the latest outcome
actions.ReleaseA: execution-owner.ts finishWork then sqlite.ts release transaction; storage retry evidence survives slot release
actions.BResultArrives: sqlite.ts indexCompletion/requestAutomatic in caller completion transaction; workspace/session/user queue and no active B input
actions.Wake/TakeWake: service.ts Queue.dropping(1), wake, Queue.take in one scanner fiber
actions.RetryReceipts/EndFailedScan: service retrySettlements attempts independent receipts, retains failed entries and combines causes; scan reports failure and continues to pending work. Legacy config restores the former scan-wide abort.
actions.ReadPending/PrepareBatch: service.ts scan running.has check and repo.prepare; sqlite.ts prepare atomically fixes membership and intent
actions.LaunchWorker/BeginB: service.ts running.add then forkIn; execution-owner.ts makeExecutionOwner and sqlite.ts begin
actions.RejectWorker/EndWorker: execution failure reporting and service.ts launch ensuring running.delete; native process life is outside this worker latch
actions.SubmitB: service.ts submit per-session/global admission, canSubmit/fence then synchronous start callback; sqlite.ts fence CAS prepared->submitting
actions.SettleB/UnknownB: execution-owner.ts finishWork observation plus sqlite.ts settle transaction; failed/ambiguous transport is not replay permission
actions.ReleaseB/ReleaseStoppedB: sqlite.ts release transaction; no submission means no result consumption; service wakes after durable slot release
actions.StopB: service.ts pause under same admission; sqlite.ts pause cancels prior input and supersedes prepared batch without deleting results

abstractionNotes: Original scheduling slice only. A is initialized in an already-submitted batch context. Repeated failed updates for the same A batch are represented by the latest retained Map entry, not one indivisible pair of writes. One B input/result only; admission and SQL fences are exact boundaries, not a claim that the whole surrounding async method is atomic. The worker latch is separate from durable active execution. No fresh-input/steer/config/host-handoff/native-process/whole-database-outage model.
